title: FEI Tribunal Final Decision C25-0039 Case 2025 FT21 DENALI QH - Mr Majed ALQAHTANI (PR)
text:
DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
24 March 2026
In the matter of
Mr. Majed ALQAHTANI- (PR: Ref. C25-0039)
(FEI Case number: 2025/FT21 DENALI QH)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Ms Diane Pitts (USA)
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0039 [FEI 2025/FT21 DENALI QH]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Majed ALQAHTANI/10363591/KSA
Trainer/ID/NF: Fahad WALEED/10306368/KSA
Event/Date: CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04.2025
Event/Code: 2025_CI_0266_E_S_02
Date of sample collection: 26.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Triamcinolone Acetonide
Bar Code Nos.: 1417731

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Mr Majed ALQAHTANI (the
PR) committed a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled
Medication Rules – The Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites
or Markers in a Horse’s Sample. The FEI notified the PR of the alleged charge in his capacity
as the Person Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not otherwise
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. The PR is an Endurance Rider from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia who competed in the
CEI1* 100 – Riyadh (KSA), held on 24-26 April 2025 (the Event), with his horse, Denali QH
(the Horse).
5. The FEI (together with the PR, the Parties), is the sole IOC-recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage and para-dressage, jumping, eventing, driving and para-driving,
endurance, and vaulting.
6. Blood samples were collected from the Horse on 26 April 2025 at the Event. The Horse’s
sample returned a positive finding for Triamcinolone Acetonide, a Prohibited Substance
under the Equine Prohibited List.
2

7. Triamcinolone Acetonide is a corticosteroid anti-inflammatory agent used in the
treatment of orthopaedic disease. It is classified as a Controlled Medication Substance
under the Equine Prohibited List.
III. Procedural background
8. On 19 May 2025, the FEI informed the PR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM
Rules (the Notification Letter).
9. In the Notification Letter, the PR was informed that he had the right to request the
Horse’s B sample to be analysed. The B-Sample analysis was not requested.
10. On 21 and 25 May 20251, the PR replied to the Notification Letter and contested that the
Sampling Procedure was improperly conducted. The PR argued that he had not been
informed of the official nature of the testing, that he signed the FEI Sampling Form
without fully understanding its content, and that he did not see the Sample being placed
in a properly secured box.
11. In an email of 29 May 2025, the PR further denied the administration of any Controlled
Medication substance, supplement, or veterinary treatment containing Triamcinolone
Acetonide, or any other Prohibited Substance to the Horse, either by himself or by any
member of his team. He reiterated that the Sample Collection Procedure had been
unclear and improperly conducted, adding that he had been asked to sign the FEI
Sampling Form before the Sample was taken and without being made aware that the
Form could later be used in a disciplinary context. He added that he did not realise the
seriousness of the situation, as it was only his second FEI competition.
12. Despite various reminders from the FEI Legal Department i.e., 24 June and 25 August
2025, no further reply was submitted by the PR, nor did the PR request a hearing.
13. In accordance with Article 8.3.6 of the ECM Rules, if the Person Responsible and/or
member of the Support Personnel (where applicable) does not elect the Administrative
Procedure within the fixed time limit, the Administrative Sanctions shall be considered
declined, and the case shall be submitted to the FEI Tribunal for final Decision.
14. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case file (the FEI’s
Response) to the Tribunal for adjudication.
1 The two emails sent on 21 and 25 May 2025 were identical in content.
3

15. On 19 December 2025, the Tribunal Chair appointed a one-person Hearing Panel (the
Panel) to decide this case. The Parties were asked to provide any objections to the
constitution of the Panel by 7 January 2026. In addition, the PR was invited to respond to
the FEI’s allegations by submitting a statement of defence and any supporting evidence
by 26 January 2026. Finally, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to
request a hearing by 29 January 2026, at the latest.
16. On 19 December 2025, the FEI confirmed having no objection to the constitution of the
Panel. The PR never replied; therefore, his silence was taken as agreement to the
constitution of the Panel..
17. The PR did not file a formal submission or request a hearing despite having been notified
of the Tribunal’s letter via email directly to him and through the Saudi NF. Therefore, the
Final Decision was rendered by the Sole Panel Member based on the papers submitted
within the deadline.
IV. The Parties’ Submissions:2
A. Submissions by the PR
18. The PR made no submissions other than the email submissions outlined in paragraphs
10 and 11 of this Decision.
B. Submissions by the FEI:
19. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted the FEI Response to the Tribunal. The FEI’s
position is summarised as follows:
19.1 Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules prohibits the presence of a Controlled Medication
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a horse's sample. As a strict
liability offence, it is not necessary that intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use
be demonstrated in order to establish an ECM Rule violation under Article 2.1.
19.2 In the present case, the analysis of the Sample confirmed the presence of
Triamcinolone Acetonide in the Horse’s system. This finding alone satisfies the
requirements of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
19.3 Article 118.3 of the GRs establishes that, “the Person Responsible shall be the
Athlete who rides […] the Horse during an Event […].” The PR is the Athlete who rode
2 The following section is a summary of the relevant facts and evidence of the Parties’ written submissions.
4

the Horse at the Event.
19.4 Article 9.1 of the ECM Rules establishes that an ECM Rule “in connection with a
Test in a given Competition automatically leads to the Disqualification of the result(s)
of the Person Responsible and Horse combination obtained in that Competition with
all resulting Consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and
prizes. […] Even if a Sanction is reduced or eliminated under Article 10 below, such
reduction or elimination does not reverse the automatic Disqualification of the
Result(s) mandated by this Article 9.“
19.5 Article 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules also provides that, “an ECM Rule violation occurring
during or in connection with an Event shall, upon the Decision of the FEI Tribunal,
lead to Disqualification of all of the Person Responsible's results obtained in that
Event, with any and all Horses, with all Consequences, including forfeiture of all
medals, points and prizes […].”
19.6 To maintain a level playing field, the FEI requests the disqualification of all the
results obtained by the PR and the Horse during the Event, in accordance with
Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules.
19.7 Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules provides that a Person Responsible with no previous
ECM Rule violation, but who violates Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, is subject to a
period of Ineligibility of six (6) months, unless they can rebut the presumption of
Fault on a balance of probability.
19.8 Therefore, in this case, to rebut the presumption of Fault, the PR must establish to
the satisfaction of the Tribunal (on a balance of probability), how the Triamcinolone
Acetonide entered the Horse’s system. The PR must also demonstrate one of the
following:
1. He bears No Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, i.e., that he did not
know or suspect, and could not reasonably have known or suspected even
with the exercise of utmost caution, that he had administered to the horse
(or the horse’s system otherwise contained) a Prohibited Substance. If
proven, the period of Ineligibility is eliminated completely pursuant to Article
10.5 of the ECM Rules.
2. He bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, in which
case, the period of Ineligibility may be reduced based on the degree of fault,
pursuant to Article 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
5

19.9 The FEI submitted that the PR must provide clear and convincing evidence that
proves how the Triamcinolone Acetonide entered the Horse’s body. In his
submissions dated 21, 25 and 29 May 2025, the PR alleged that the Sample
Collection Procedure was unclear and improperly conducted. In particular, the
PR argued that: (i) he had not been informed of the official nature of the testing
nor of the procedural implications of signing the FEI Sampling Form; (ii) he had
been requested to sign the FEI Sampling Form prior to the Sample being taken;
and (iii) the full sampling protocol had not been followed in his presence, as he
was asked to leave immediately after the Sample was collected and therefore
did not witness the Sample being placed and sealed in a properly secured box.
19.10 In relation to point (i), the FEI submitted that the PR bore the legal responsibility
for the Horse, including responsibility under the GRs and Veterinary Regulations
(the VRs), and was liable under the applicable FEI Legal Regulations. It was also
the obligation of the PR, as well as of every person subject to the Statutes, GRs
and Sport Rules, to be familiar with these provisions, and ignorance of them
does not exempt any person from liability.
19.11 In relation to points (ii) and (iii), the FEI highlighted that the PR duly signed the
FEI Sampling Form. The FEI Sampling Form expressly included the following
assertion: “I certify that I supervised the collection and sealing of the undermentioned
sample in accordance with the FEI Veterinary Regulations.” By signing this form, the
PR confirmed that the Sample Collection and sealing were properly conducted
in accordance with the applicable procedures. The FEI further noted that the PR
had the opportunity to record any alleged deviation from the Sampling
Procedure directly on the FEI Sampling Form. However, no such remark was ever
made. Consequently, the signed FEI Sampling Form and absence of any
recorded objection directly contradicted the PR’s allegation that the Sampling
Procedure was not properly conducted or supervised. In addition, the FEI further
confirmed with the Testing Veterinarian, Dr. Khaled AKL, that the name and
signature included in the FEI Sampling Form did correspond to the PR, and that
the PR was present during the complete Sampling Procedure.
20. The FEI also submitted that pursuant to Article 3.2.3 of the ECM Rules, “departures from
any provision of these Rules shall not invalidate analytical results or other evidence of an ECM
Rule violation; provided, however, that if the Person Responsible and/or member of the Support
Personnel and/or other Person establishes that a departure from a provision of these ECM
Rules could reasonably have caused the ECM Rule violation based on the Adverse Analytical
Finding or other ECM Rule violation, then the FEI shall have the burden to establish that such
departure did not cause the Adverse Analytical Finding or the factual basis for the ECM Rule
violation”.
6

21. In the present case, the FEI confirmed their opinion that the PR had failed to establish
the first requirement i.e., (a) the alleged procedural irregularities which subsequently
failed to establish the second requirement i.e., (b) that such alleged procedural
irregularities could reasonably have caused the ECM Rule violation in question.
Furthermore, the FEI noted that allegations require substantiating evidence. The FEI
noted that no evidence whatsoever has been submitted by the PR to demonstrate that
the alleged departures occurred and could have reasonably caused the Adverse
Analytical Finding.
22. Therefore, it was the FEI’s opinion that the burden of proof had not shifted to the FEI in
the sense of the above provision and that the Analytical Finding stands unopposed.
23. The FEI therefore considers that the source of the Adverse Analytical Finding has not
been established. As to Fault/Negligence for the Rule Violation, the starting point of any
evaluation is the “personal duty” of the PR following from Article 2.1.1 of the ECM Rules,
i.e., his personal duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication Substance is present in
the Horse’s body during an Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” It is also the
responsibility of the PR to rebut the presumption of Fault and to submit all relevant
arguments regarding the source of the Prohibited Substance, as well as any allegations
that he or she bears No (Significant) Fault or Negligence in relation to its presence.
24. In the present case, the PR has failed to respond to the charges brought forward by the
FEI. Consequently, it remained impossible, under the applicable rules, to evaluate the
PR’s degree of Fault or Negligence, if any. Consequently, the presumption of Fault as
stipulated in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules remains.
25. The FEI also stated that no elimination or reduction of the period of Ineligibility in this
case is possible and the applicable sanction for the current violation should be 6 (six)
months of Ineligibility in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules.
26. The FEI respectfully requested that the Tribunal issue a decision:
(i) upholding the charge that the PR has violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules;
(ii) imposing a period of Ineligibility of six (6) months on the PR, commencing from
the date of the Final Decision in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iii) disqualifying the result of the PR and Horse combination obtained in the Event,
and the consequent forfeiture of all medals, points, prize money, etc. won,
pursuant to Article 9 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iv) fining the PR in the amount of 3’500 CHF;
(v) ordering the PR to pay the legal costs of 2’000 CHF that the FEI has incurred in
these proceedings.
V. Legal Analysis
7

A. Jurisdiction
27. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member
of the Saudi NF, which is a member of the FEI; therefore, the PR is bound by the ECM
Rules.
B. Legal Discussion
28. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
29. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the Sample reflects that the analytical tests were performed
in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal is further satisfied
that the test results evidence the presence of Triamcinolone Acetonide in the Sample taken
from the Horse at the Event. Triamcinolone Acetonide is a Controlled Medication
Substance and the presence of this substance in a horse’s system is prohibited under Article
2.1 of the ECM Rules.
30. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Tribunal notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the
PR committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to
prove intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
31. The burden of proof then shifts to the PR. The standard of proof for the PR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the PR
to escape a six (6) month sanction, he must establish, on a balance of probability: (i) how
the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and that (ii) he bears No
(Significant) Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
ii. Controlled Medication Rule Violation
8

32. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Triamcinolone Acetonide in the Horse’s
system, which constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore, the FEI
satisfied its burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the
objective elements of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
iii. Elimination or Reduction of the Period of Ineligibility
33. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules. To benefit from
a reduction, the PR must establish, as a threshold requirement, how the Prohibited
Substance entered the Horse’s system.3
34. Other than blanket denials, the PR did not submit any evidence establishing how the
Prohibited Substance entered into the Horse’s system. Therefore, the Tribunal finds that
the PR did not discharge his burden of proving how the Prohibited Substance entered
into the Horse’s system. The Tribunal therefore considers that the source of the Adverse
Analytical Finding has not been established.
35. The starting point of any evaluation is the “personal duty” of the PR following from Article
2.1.1 of the ECM Rules, i.e., his personal duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication
Substance is present in the Horse’s body during an Event without a valid Veterinary
Form.” It is the responsibility of the PR to rebut the presumption of Fault and to submit
all relevant arguments regarding the source of the Prohibited Substance, as well as any
allegations that he or she bears No (Significant) Fault or Negligence in relation to its
presence. In the present case, the PR has failed to respond to the charges brought
forward by the FEI. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the PR is not entitled to any
reduction of the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of
the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
3 FEI Tribunal Decisions: C23-0031 [FEI 2023/FT12 – ALASOUF] dated 12 October 2023, C23-0034 [FEI 2023/CM05
– SAHM II] dated 8 September 2023, C23-0045 [FEI 2023/FT24 – DIFF LOOK] dated 2 November 2023, C23-0046
[2023/CM08 BALLON PARIS] dated 6 December 2023.
9

36. As the threshold criteria of source has not been proven, the Tribunal finds that the
applicable period of Ineligibility is six (6) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules,
which shall commence on the date of notification of this decision.
37. Pursuant to Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules, the results of the PR and the Horse
combination obtained in the entire Event are automatically disqualified, including
forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes.
38. The Tribunal also finds that given the PR’s apparent overall inexperience and lack of
experience with the process, that no purpose is served in imposing a large fine or legal
costs in this case. The Tribunal imposes a fine of CHF 2’000 on the PR and each party
will bear its own legal costs. If the PR’s stated financial circumstances are valid, the
Tribunal urges the FEI to work with the PR to develop a plan for payment of the fine.
VI. Terms of the Decision
39. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Mr ALQAHTANI violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
b) Mr ALQAHTANI is suspended for a period of six (6) months. The period of the
Ineligibility will be effective from the date of notification of this decision.
c) Mr ALQAHTANI’s results at the Event with the Horse are disqualified, including the
forfeiture of any prize money, medals and ranking points.
d) Mr ALQAHTANI is ordered to pay a fine of two thousand Swiss Francs (CHF 2000).
e) Each party will bear its own legal costs.
40. Mr ALQAHTANI, the Saudi NF and the FEI will be notified this Decision.
41. Mr ALQAHTANI may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in any capacity in a
Competition or activity that is authorised or organised by the FEI or any National
Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is authorized or
organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any capacity in
Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level event
organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
10

42. If Mr ALQAHTANI violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph during the
period of Ineligibility, the results of any such participation will be disqualified and a new
period of Ineligibility equal in length up to the original period of Ineligibility will be added
to the end of the original period of Ineligibility. In addition, further sanctions may be
imposed if appropriate (Article 10.13.3 of the ECM Rules).
43. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
44. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
the present notification.
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
Ms Diane Pitts, Sole Panel Member
